active_inquiry.closure_condition: Close after a fresh candidate implementing the specified velocity-aware braking/hold-margin change is archived and measured on a non-overlapping held-out panel under the official 6–20 cm distribution with the established reach/hold, qvel/action, branch, target-geometry, contact, and internal-step diagnostics. A positive conclusion requires at least 157/160 successes (the panel-equivalent 98% threshold), preserved or improved first-reach coverage, and materially reduced hold interruptions/internal excursions without a new concentrated failure class. A limited or negative conclusion is sufficient if success remains below 157/160 or the diagnostics show persistent target-angle/route-conditioned non-reach, torque saturation, or hold instability; that result will determine whether to continue policy/control development or redirect toward route/observability/learning-recipe investigation. Protected official continuous-hold semantics remain unresolved and will not be claimed from development traces.
active_inquiry.goal_connection: The only measured learned candidate achieved 150/160 = 93.75%, leaving a 4.25 percentage-point development gap to the 98% goal. Seven failures lacked first reach and three reached but failed the hold; the latter had near-tolerance qvel norms of 6.05 and 7.31 rad/s, saturated action magnitude 1.414, and 192/242 internal boundary excursions, while all failures were contact-free. A targeted learned-control intervention could therefore change complete episode capability, and its diagnostic outcome could redirect the campaign if reach remains angle-conditioned or hold remains unstable. The open branch produced all observed reaches, so branch nonuse alone is not treated as a deficit requiring folded-route forcing.
active_inquiry.handoff_conclusion:
Established observations: M1 verified the compiled two-joint plant, 0.002 s internal integration, ten internal steps per 20 ms action, and substantial torque authority in tested traces; those traces had no contacts. M2 verified exposure to the full official 6–20 cm radial range. T1's training proxy improved through 120,832 actual steps, but proxies and terminal status do not establish development performance. M3, M5, and M7 measured the frozen terminal artifact on the same 160-episode panel at 150/160. M7 records seven non-reach failures and three reached-but-unstable hold failures; the latter combine high near-tolerance velocity, saturated action, repeated interruptions, and internal excursions. The policy reached only the open elbow branch, yet it succeeded in 150 episodes, so branch nonuse is not evidence that folded-branch coverage is required.

Interpretation: the tested PPO artifact has a consequential policy-timing/braking and complete-hold limitation, with a separate reach limitation in seven episodes. The zero-contact result and M1 authority traces weaken generic contact and generic insufficient-authority explanations, but do not exclude target-angle-, singularity-, route-, or saturation-conditioned failures. The model's torque-control and singular-start consequences make velocity-aware braking and margin-aware hold behavior physically credible targets. Internal excursions demonstrate development fragility, not an official continuous-hold failure, because protected evaluator semantics are unresolved.

Correction to the inherited direction: I do not retain explicit folded-branch coverage as a primary intervention. The evidence establishes no folded-route comparison and shows the open route can succeed; forcing a second branch could add an untested failure mode without addressing the observed gap. I retain route/target-conditioned diagnostics as a discriminator: persistent angle-conditioned non-reach or saturation would redirect the next direction, whereas lower velocity and interruption rates with preserved reach would support continued policy/control development. Claims remain limited to this PPO recipe, interface, and measured panel.

request.current_synthesis: Observed evidence from completed M1: the independent verification passed analytic planar forward kinematics (maximum error 2.78e-17 m), zero-action zero-velocity invariance over 40 internal updates, repeated held-control traces with 30 samples and 29 changing updates per reset, and detection of two deliberately constructed interior tolerance excursions that boundary-only sampling would miss. The operative compiled model measured nq=nv=nu=2, timestep 0.002 s, 10 internal steps per 20 ms control interval, diagonal free-space dof_M0 values 0.01210 and 0.01019, damping and armature 0.5 and 0.01, gear 5, control range [-1,1], and no actuator force limit. In deterministic held unit-torque traces, joint speeds reached about 9.6-9.7 rad/s within 80 ms; zero-action decay from [0.8,-0.5] rad/s reduced to [0.0133,-0.0030] rad/s over 100 ms; tested traces had zero contacts. These observations support the interpretation that motion authority is ample and that overshoot/braking and hold robustness are more consequential initial mechanisms than inability to reach. The near-tolerance controlled trace reached a minimum of 8.5 mm but exceeded 10 mm at both control boundaries and at 28 internal samples, demonstrating that the tested trajectory was not a successful hold and that sampled and internal behavior can differ. Competing explanation A, a compiled-dynamics authority bottleneck, is weakened for the tested configurations but not excluded across all target geometry or policy routes. Explanation B, a learned-policy timing/braking/hold bottleneck, is now the leading development hypothesis, but it is untested because no policy was evaluated. Continuous protected evaluator semantics remain unknown; the synthetic check validates only the analysis capability, not the hidden evaluator.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is whether the first capability intervention should develop a learned policy under the existing torque interface with explicit braking/hold-sensitive diagnostics, or whether a broader physical route/contact/geometry investigation is needed first. Evidence that would redirect away from policy development would include target- or branch-conditioned torque-step failures, contact impulses, actuator saturation/force behavior inconsistent with the compiled facts, or systematic inability to settle even under a competent feedback trajectory. Evidence that would support policy-focused development would be a candidate that reaches targets but loses the hold, shows high near-tolerance qdot or internal excursions, or fails by target geometry while the compiled model remains contact-free and dynamically authoritative. The official evaluator's continuous-versus-boundary rule is still unavailable, so any development candidate must be judged with internal traces or conservative margin rather than aggregate sampled success alone.

pi_checkpoint.current_goal_gap: T1:checkpoint-120832 achieved 150/160 = 93.75% on a held-out development panel, versus the panel-equivalent 98% threshold of 157/160 and the official requirement of 196/200. Seven failures lacked first reach and three reached but did not complete the hold. The hold failures had 192 and 242 boundary-in-tolerance internal excursions, near-tolerance qvel norms of 6.05 and 7.31 rad/s, and saturated action magnitude 1.414. All ten failures had zero contacts. The protected evaluator's exact continuous-versus-sampled hold semantics remain unavailable.
pi_checkpoint.current_synthesis:
Established observations: M1 verified the compiled two-joint plant, 0.002 s internal integration, ten internal steps per 20 ms action, and substantial torque authority in tested traces; those traces had no contacts. M2 verified exposure to the full official 6–20 cm radial range. T1's training proxy improved through 120,832 actual steps, but proxies and terminal status do not establish development performance. M3, M5, and M7 measured the frozen terminal artifact on the same 160-episode panel at 150/160. M7 records seven non-reach failures and three reached-but-unstable hold failures; the latter combine high near-tolerance velocity, saturated action, repeated interruptions, and internal excursions. The policy reached only the open elbow branch, yet it succeeded in 150 episodes, so branch nonuse is not evidence that folded-branch coverage is required.

Interpretation: the tested PPO artifact has a consequential policy-timing/braking and complete-hold limitation, with a separate reach limitation in seven episodes. The zero-contact result and M1 authority traces weaken generic contact and generic insufficient-authority explanations, but do not exclude target-angle-, singularity-, route-, or saturation-conditioned failures. The model's torque-control and singular-start consequences make velocity-aware braking and margin-aware hold behavior physically credible targets. Internal excursions demonstrate development fragility, not an official continuous-hold failure, because protected evaluator semantics are unresolved.

Correction to the inherited direction: I do not retain explicit folded-branch coverage as a primary intervention. The evidence establishes no folded-route comparison and shows the open route can succeed; forcing a second branch could add an untested failure mode without addressing the observed gap. I retain route/target-conditioned diagnostics as a discriminator: persistent angle-conditioned non-reach or saturation would redirect the next direction, whereas lower velocity and interruption rates with preserved reach would support continued policy/control development. Claims remain limited to this PPO recipe, interface, and measured panel.
pi_checkpoint.decision_frontier: Can a fresh learned torque policy with explicit velocity-aware braking and a complete-hold margin objective raise complete development success to at least 157/160 while preserving first reach, or do target-angle/route-conditioned non-reach and saturation persist? Evidence that hold interruptions, near-tolerance qvel/action, and internal excursions fall while reach is preserved supports continuing learned policy/control development. Reach improvement without hold improvement isolates stabilization as the remaining bottleneck. Persistent angle-conditioned non-reach with saturation, or a new route-conditioned deficit, redirects toward route/observability or learning-recipe investigation. Because official continuous-hold semantics are unavailable, internal-step excursions remain a conservative robustness discriminator and cannot alone certify or reject the official goal.
